speaker: Unknown
en: So that's certainly number one.

speaker: Unknown
en: But as a close second, I think something that especially founders have appreciated, not so much institutional investors, but founders, is that we don't sell the companies we buy.

speaker: Unknown
en: So they know that with us, the company has probably a forever own, and they've seen how much we can invest in the product and make the product better.

speaker: Unknown
en: And many founders feel a sense of attachment, even legacy connected with the products they helped develop.

en: And so knowing that they're selling their business, including...

en: So when we start an acquisition, we always start from some very solid basis on which we believe we can.
zh: 当我们开始一笔收购时，我们总是从一些非常扎实的基础出发，我们相信我们可以，

speaker: Unknown
en: you know help the business grow where we see very you know untapped potential.

speaker: Unknown
en: And we really try to map out everything that there is to know about the business.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

en: But talking with their team and understanding the acquisition, no, it was a very healthy company.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: So we A-B test everything we release because we never want opinions to get in the way of success.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the issue most of the time is that while obsessing on perfection, people miss so many opportunities to get things done and testing things.
zh: 我认为大多数时候的问题在于,在追求完美的过程中,人们错过了太多把事情完成和进行测试的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think the analysis paralysis, especially when it comes to, for example, code deploy or infrastructural design, those things can really slow down a product.
zh: 所以我认为分析瘫痪,尤其是当涉及到,比如说,代码部署或基础设施设计时,这些事情真的会拖慢一个产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you need very

en: And sometimes companies, just because they become bigger and bigger, they tend to overweight themselves with these processes and approvals and inability to really run the business.
